findings.title: Search for "login" does not match "Issue with log-in": punctuation becomes a space instead of being removed
findings.requirement: specs/features/11-search-board.md Scenario: Search matching is case insensitive and normalizes whitespace and punctuation ("login" must match "Login fails" and "Issue with log-in")
findings.evidence: Still reproduces. Re-run of prev/specs/11-search.spec.ts: 11-S3 and 11-S3c fail (row count 0 for the log-in title; query "log-in" does not match "Login fails"). Screenshots and traces: evidence/functional/test-results/prev/11-search-11-search-11-S3--*/ and .../11-search-11-search-punctu-*/. Log: evidence/functional/prev-run-log.txt. The shipped tests/search/search.spec.ts:30 guards it with test.fail, which records the defect but does not cover the fix.
findings.repro: Create a bug titled "Issue with log-in", log in as buggy, type "login" in the search field: the bug is not shown.
findings.fix: In normalizeForSearch, remove punctuation instead of replacing it: lower.replace(/\p{P}/gu, "")

findings.title: Empty-board and all-open-board scenarios cannot be run against the shared database
findings.requirement: specs/features/07-bug-board.md Scenario: Board page shows an empty table when there are no bugs; specs/features/13-bug-status.md Scenario: No bugs matched message when selected state has no bugs
findings.evidence: Still a gap. The shipped suite says so in comments: bug-board has no empty-board test, and bug-status uses a Closed plus search proxy, which passes. The "No bugs." placeholder row (BoardPage.tsx:258) was not observed in this run either.
findings.fix: Provide an isolated test database (for example a per-run DB file) so these scenarios can run deterministically

findings.title: Create-bug modal first renders the previous draft (and a blank Owner), then resets after paint, so early input is overwritten
findings.requirement: specs/features/06-create-bug.md Scenario: Create-bug modal defaults owner to the current user; specs/testing/create-bug-test-plan.md 1.5 (P-1)
findings.evidence: Still reproduces. (a) Open New Bug and clear Owner at once: 500ms later Owner reads "buggy" (gaps/specs/create-gaps.spec.ts:38). (b) Type "stale draft", blank Owner, Escape, reopen: in the first read after the click, Title is "stale draft" and Owner is "" (create-gaps.spec.ts:23). The component stays mounted, so its state survives closing, and the reset runs in a passive useEffect after paint. Screenshots: evidence/functional/test-results/gaps/create-gaps-C1-5-*/ and create-gaps-functional-04-*/.
findings.fix: Render the modal only when it is open ({createModalOpen && <CreateBugModal .../>}) and initialise with useState(defaultOwner), so the first paint is already clean

findings.title: Shipped BoardPage 'Logout' and 'New Bug' locators are not exact, so any bug whose title contains those words breaks 20 tests
findings.requirement: specs/engineering/test-automation-patterns.md (independent tests, no shared state); run rule: other agents change data concurrently
findings.evidence: Board rows are role=button, and their accessible name is the row text. getByRole('button', { name: 'Logout' }) is a substring match, so it also resolves to rows. While an exploratory agent's bug "[exploratory] R03 after-logout ..." was on the board, 4 of 9 tests in tests/logout, tests/login/session.spec.ts and tests/title-bar failed with a strict-mode violation. With my own bug "[functional] New Bug Logout collision probe" present, 20 of 26 tests in tests/title-bar, tests/login/session.spec.ts, tests/logout and tests/create-bug failed: 16 on 'New Bug' resolving to 2 elements, and the rest on 'Logout'. Log: evidence/functional/suite-locator-collision-log.txt. The lead's green run depends on no such title existing at the time.
findings.repro: POST a bug titled "[x] New Bug Logout", then npx playwright test tests/title-bar tests/create-bug --project=chromium --workers=1
findings.fix: Scope and pin both locators: this.header.getByRole('button', { name: 'New Bug', exact: true }) and this.header.getByRole('button', { name: 'Logout', exact: true })

findings.title: Two shipped tests assert less than their titles or scenarios claim
findings.requirement: specs/features/02-user-accounts.md (default user buggy with password 1970beetle); specs/features/12-delete-bug.md Scenario: Canceling the confirmation modal leaves the bug intact ("And the board still displays the bug")
findings.evidence: users-file 'the default buggy account exists' checks only the username, not the password the spec names. delete-bug 'cancelling the confirmation...' checks the edit modal and the API but never checks the board row. I checked the board row myself (gaps/specs/edit-delete-gaps.spec.ts '12-S4', pass). The other sampled tests assert what their titles say.
findings.fix: Add expect(users.find(u => u.username === 'buggy')?.password).toBe('1970beetle'), and after cancelling, close the edit modal and expect boardPage.rowCount(bug.title) to be 1
